name: Sysrepo
what_it_is: Sysrepo is a YANG-based configuration and operational state data store for Unix/Linux applications, providing ACID-like transaction guarantees and integrating with management agents such as NETCONF and RESTCONF servers.
components: sysrepoctl CLI — manages installed YANG modules and their permissions
sysrepo-plugind — daemon providing systemd service support
JSON DS file plugin (default datastore backend)
MONGO DS plugin (requires libmongoc ≥1.24.0 + MongoDB server)
REDIS DS plugin (requires libhiredis ≥1.1.0 + Redis Stack)
Shared memory (SHM) layer for inter-process context sharing
measurement: sr_perf tool measures execution time for common use-cases with large YANG instance data
Code coverage via ENABLE_COVERAGE=ON CMake flag (gcov/lcov/genhtml)
Cmocka-based unit tests with optional Valgrind integration
configuration: REPO_PATH CMake variable — custom repository location
SR_PLUGINS_PATH CMake variable — DS and NTF plugins location
SYSREPO_UMASK / SYSREPO_GROUP — file permission security settings
NACM_RECOVERY_USER CMake variable — recovery account (default: root)
DEFAULT_*_DS_PLG CMake variables — datastore plugin assignment per datastore type
MONGO_HOST, MONGO_PORT, MONGO_USERNAME, MONGO_PASSWORD, MONGO_AUTHSOURCE — MongoDB backend config
REDIS_HOST, REDIS_PORT, REDIS_USERNAME, REDIS_PASSWORD — Redis backend config
SYSREPO_REPOSITORY_PATH env var — runtime repository path override
SYSREPO_SHM_PREFIX env var — isolates multiple sysrepo instances on the same machine
SYSREPO_SHM_DIR env var — relocates shared memory directory
SR_ENV_RUN_TESTS env var — enables package tests without privilege elevation
PRINTED_CONTEXT_ADDRESS — shared YANG context memory address (enabled by default on Linux 4.17+)
modes: startup datastore — persists configuration across reboots
candidate datastore — staging area for proposed configuration changes
operational datastore — runtime state and operational data published by applications
devel branch — tested improvements ahead of stable
constraints: No master process: cannot enforce centralized access control; relies entirely on filesystem permissions
C language only natively; Python and C++ bindings are separate projects
ASLR may need to be disabled on systems without MAP_FIXED_NOREPLACE for printed context to work
Full CLI is available only as separate projects (not bundled)
Schema mount inline mount points must share parent YANG context
Default permissions allow no users other than the recovery user to write data until explicitly configured
Local processes can break sysrepo by manipulating shared files — not safe against malicious local processes
notable_absences: No docker-compose file in the repository
No fault injection or chaos testing mechanisms documented
No built-in metrics or monitoring endpoint
No encryption at rest for stored datastore data
No role-based access control beyond NACM user-based controls
